Published online:
    September 2, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States (with broader global context: Iran conflict, global bond issuance)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES]

Synopsis:
    A Reuters poll of FX strategists finds the dollar likely to hold firm near-term but weaken over a year. Key drivers: sparse Fed guidance under Chair Kevin Warsh (seen as neither clearly hawkish nor dovish), markets pricing two Fed hikes to combat inflation running near 4%, but most strategists skeptical the Fed will tighten as aggressively as priced. Additional pressures include a 10-year Treasury yield near 4.82%, US debt topping $40 trillion, an August Treasury buyback surprise, and a US-Iran military flare-up. Dollar long positioning is declining. FX forecasters see EUR/USD at $1.16–$1.18 over the next year, with slightly more than half flagging downside dollar risk relative to their forecasts.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — directly addresses Fed rate path, Treasury yields at near 3-year highs, dollar positioning, and market rate pricing.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 65 (markets are currently pricing two hikes, making rate increases a central narrative)
Probability of increase: 40% (markets price it in, but majority of strategists and cited economists doubt the Fed follows through to that extent)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 30 (implicit undercurrent — strategists expect fewer hikes than priced, suggesting rates may be closer to a hold than markets assume)
Probability of holding: 25% (possible but not the dominant scenario given inflation near 4% and hawkish market pricing)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 20 (Reinhart explicitly argues Fed will not tighten as priced, implying rates end up lower than market expectations, though outright cuts are not discussed)
Probability of decrease: 15% (no direct cut discussion; strategists lean against full hike pricing but stop short of calling for cuts)

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: +20 (Mildly hawkish lean — Warsh's recent remarks were described as relatively hawkish, the 10-year hit a near 3-year high of 4.82%, and markets are pricing two hikes; however, dominant expert view is that actual Fed tightening will undershoot current pricing, capping the hawkish read)
